sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|magic damage}} to an enemy champion with a [[champion ability]] applies a stack of ''Vile Decay'' ... Each stack inflicts {{as|{{fd|7.5}}% magic resistance reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|mr}} at 4 stacks. — note this is a RESISTANCE effect, not a damage multiplier; it must never surface as a support_damage_multiplier.
post = raw · m(R), m(R) = 100/(100+R); mitigation is linear in raw, so damage-taken amplifiers compose as scalar multipliers on the raw term and commute with mitigation and with expectation.

rule_derived_from_sources: Abyssal Mask — Unmake (S1, S2, S3): a curse on the enemy champion; amplifies MAGIC damage only, by exactly 12% (x1.12); applies to damage 'from all sources' (any ally, any ability/auto/item-proc/DoT tick), has NO duration and NO cooldown, and is gated only by (a) target is an enemy champion, (b) target is within 700 units of the Abyssal holder.
Imperial Mandate — Command (S4): x1.07 on ALL damage types, but only inside a 4 s Vulnerable window opened by an immobilize (refreshable).
Bloodletter's Curse — Vile Decay (S5): %MR reduction, belongs in the resistance term m(R), NOT in a damage multiplier.
Composition (S6): independent damage-taken amps are scalar multipliers on raw damage and compose multiplicatively.
independent_computation.arithmetic: 1.12 x 1.07 = 1.1984; 12% and 7% are independent multiplicative amps, never additive (1.19 would be the wrong composition).
independent_computation.conclusion: The old leaf {1.12, 'Abyssal Mask — Unmake'} is the correct value on one and only one class of event: a MAGIC-damage event with Mandate's Vulnerable window inactive. On a physical or true damage event the Unmake amp must not appear at all — S1/S2 restrict it to 'magic damage', and S3 confirms the cached decomposition types it as damage.magic. For the leaf to be correctly absent, events[21] must be non-magic damage (or the amp must have been re-homed to a differently-named merged-amp field carrying the same 1.12 on magic events).

why_this_verdict: Game truth is unambiguous and narrow: Unmake is a MAGIC-ONLY amplifier (S1 wiki + S2 Riot text agree; S3 types the atom as damage.magic). Any event whose damage is physical or true must carry no Unmake multiplier.

The roster under test deliberately pairs an all-damage-type amp (Imperial Mandate Command, 7%, S4) with a magic-only amp (Abyssal Unmake, 12%, S1) and a %MR shred (Bloodletter's Curse Vile Decay, S5). The only reason to build that particular three-item roster is to assert that the magic-only amp drops off non-magic events while the all-type amp does not, and that the MR shred stays in the resistance term. A single Abyssal-only multiplier disappearing from one event is exactly the signature of that type gate landing correctly.

The opposite reading (a regression that deletes the support amp wholesale) would have to delete the leaf on magic events too, i.e. produce a uniform 1.12-→-absent sweep rather than a per-event drop, and would leave magic events with no amp at all — which is not what a single-leaf change looks like.

A third possible reading — the amp being re-homed into a merged multi-source amp field — also makes the absence of THIS leaf path correct, provided the 12% still reaches magic events through the new field. Two of the three readings land on new_value_correct.

residual_uncertainty.not_determinable_from_the_evidence_tree: The evidence tree (data/ + docs/math-foundations.md) contains no scenario definition and no golden output, so the damage TYPE of combat/events[21] cannot be observed from it. grep for 'support_damage_multiplier' and 'mandate_abyssal' over the whole export returns zero hits; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json holds 22 unrelated scenarios and none of the support-aura roster family.
residual_uncertainty.falsifier: If combat/events[21] deals MAGIC damage (an ability part, a magic on-hit, or a magic DoT/burn tick) to an enemy champion within 700 units of the Abyssal holder, AND no other leaf on that event carries the 12% amp, then the correct value is x1.12 and this verdict flips to old_value_correct.
residual_uncertainty.second_falsifier: If events[21] is magic damage AND Mandate's Vulnerable window is active there, then neither value is right: the correct multiplier is 1.12 x 1.07 = 1.1984 and the verdict is both_wrong.
residual_uncertainty.cheapest_check_for_the_orchestrator: Read the damage_type / source of combat/events[21] in the baseline. magic → flip to old_value_correct (or both_wrong if Vulnerable is active); physical or true → this verdict stands.

asides: Bloodletter's Curse (item 8010) must never contribute to support_damage_multiplier — Vile Decay is 7.5%-per-stack MAGIC RESISTANCE REDUCTION (max 30% at 4 stacks), which belongs inside m(R) = 100/(100+R). If any leaf in this scenario attributes a multiplier to Vile Decay, that is a separate defect regardless of this leaf's outcome.

If a merged amp field now composes Mandate + Abyssal, verify it multiplies (1.1984) rather than adding (1.19); docs/math-foundations.md § 2.1 establishes that amps are scalar factors on raw damage, so additive stacking would be wrong.
